lines.trans: Believe me, I do not want to lose you anymore.
I do!
Lena, some kind of mistake happened.
That is not what I meant.
I bought a pendant, you see, and not this ring!
It turned out funny.
The evening was wonderful.
Lena, wait, hear me out!
There is no need to explain anything.
It is not for nothing that people recommend you! So pleasant.
Who put a ring in here?!
My back is completely better, thank you!

lines.trans: Some kind of mistake happened!

meanings.note: Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (stem 'верить'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'believe, trust', paired with 'верить'.

examples.trans: And everyone believed it?
Believe me.

examples.text: Со своего телефона? И все поверили?
examples.trans: From your own phone? And everyone believed it?

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'I', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: They say that thoughts are material.

examples.text: Если о чём-то постоянно думать, это обязательно произойдёт.
examples.trans: If you think about something constantly, it will definitely happen.

examples.text: Звони в любое время! Ладно, я пойду.
examples.trans: Call at any time! Alright, I will go.

meanings.note: Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.

examples.trans: And besides massage, anything intimate?
We've done a lot.
Too much to do.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian discourse particle adding conversational nuance meaning 'not', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Well, do not stay silent.
Can you bring me something?
Yes, of course!

meanings.note: Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'want', paired with 'захотеть'.

examples.text: Понимаю, гормоны шалят. Я просто захотела тушёнки!
examples.trans: I understand, hormones are acting up. I simply wanted stewed meat!
Chef! I wanted to bring you some tea.

examples.text: Шеф, мы вас ждём. Мы просто хотели, чтобы вы нам помогли.
examples.trans: Chef, we are waiting for you. We just wanted you to help us.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'you', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Max, why are you here?

examples.text: Ты забыла? У вас послезавтра развод!
examples.trans: Did you forget? Your divorce is the day after tomorrow!

examples.text: Знаешь что, давай ты лучше дома переночуешь.
examples.trans: You know what, you had better spend the night at home.

meanings.note: Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to lose', paired with 'потерять'.

examples.text: Поверь, я больше не хочу тебя терять.
examples.trans: Believe me, I do not want to lose you anymore.

examples.text: Мы ваш подарок потеряли и купили кольцо.
examples.trans: We lost your gift and bought a ring.
You're wasting your time.

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'огласный'). Adjective formed with the common Slavic suffix '-н-' from a noun/verb root. Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('agreeable, agree').

examples.trans: I do!
I agree.
I agree to this bet!

meanings.note: Prefix 'про-' indicates movement through, completion, or missing the mark (stem 'изойти'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'occurred, there was', paired with 'происходить'.

examples.text: Если о чём-то постоянно думать, это обязательно произойдёт.
examples.trans: If you think about something constantly, it will definitely happen.
Perhaps a miracle will happen.
What happened?

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'some kind of', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: What nonsense.
Some man called you.

examples.text: Бред какой-то. Но, с другой стороны, чем я рискую?
examples.trans: What nonsense. But on the other hand, what have I got to lose?

meanings.note: Common feminine noun meaning 'freak' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: И я обещаю больше никогда не делать глупых ошибок.
examples.trans: And I promise never to make foolish mistakes again.
Lena, some kind of mistake happened.
Some kind of mistake happened!

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'this, it (is)', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Если о чём-то постоянно думать, это обязательно произойдёт.
examples.trans: If you think about something constantly, it will definitely happen.

examples.text: Слушай, ты можешь отключить этот противный звук?
examples.trans: Listen, can you turn off that annoying sound?
Vitya, this is a fiasco!

meanings.note: Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'had'.

examples.trans: Precisely, a surprise!

examples.text: Но вы не волнуйтесь. Массаж снимет боль, и боли в спине пройдут.
examples.trans: But do not worry. The massage will relieve the ache, and the back pains will pass.
Vika said that she would book a room.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian spatial or relational preposition meaning 'in, into', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: They say that thoughts are material.
Hello, Vika?
Can you bring me something?

meanings.note: Common masculine noun meaning 'mind' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: I do not even want to see you!
Well we will see tonight!
I saw a ring box.

meanings.note: Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (stem 'купать'). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'bought, was buying', paired with 'купить'.

examples.trans: And what did he buy?

examples.text: Я покупал кулон, понимаешь, а не это кольцо!
examples.trans: I bought a pendant, you see, and not this ring!
What, are you buying me?

meanings.note: Common masculine noun meaning 'pendant' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Я покупал кулон, понимаешь, а не это кольцо!
examples.trans: I bought a pendant, you see, and not this ring!

examples.text: Ну, скажите мне, почему вместо кулона появилось кольцо?
examples.trans: Well, tell me, why did a ring appear instead of a pendant?

meanings.note: Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (stem 'нимать'). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to understand', paired with 'понять'.

examples.text: Понимаю, гормоны шалят. Я просто захотела тушёнки!
examples.trans: I understand, hormones are acting up. I simply wanted stewed meat!
Vika, I understand your condition.

examples.text: Я покупал кулон, понимаешь, а не это кольцо!
examples.trans: I bought a pendant, you see, and not this ring!

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian clause-linking conjunction meaning 'and, but', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: They say that thoughts are material.

examples.text: Если о чём-то постоянно думать, это обязательно произойдёт.
examples.trans: If you think about something constantly, it will definitely happen.
Hello, Vika?

meanings.note: Common neuter noun meaning 'ring' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: I saw a ring box.
A necklace, earrings, a chain.
Or a ring! I am serious.

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'мешно'). Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.

examples.trans: It turned out funny.
Do you find it funny?
That's very funny.

meanings.en: to turn out, to work out
meanings.note: Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (stem 'лучиться'). Reflexive/intransitive verb with the postfix '-ся'/'-сь' (historically from the reflexive pronoun 'себя', oneself). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'turned out', paired with 'получаться'.

examples.trans: It will all work out!
He'll make a good doctor.

examples.text: Классный из тебя мэр получится, Самсон.
examples.trans: You'll make a great mayor, Samson.

meanings.note: Common masculine noun meaning 'evening' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: What are the plans for the evening?

examples.text: А ты не можешь потерпеть до вечера!
examples.trans: And you cannot be patient until evening!
Well we will see tonight!

meanings.note: Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'was'.

examples.trans: I have a toy car.
Childhood was hard.
You will be asking for forgiveness.

meanings.note: Adjective formed with the common Slavic suffix '-н-' from a noun/verb root. Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('wonderful, marvelous').

examples.trans: The evening was wonderful.
This is wonderful caviar.
Listen, this is wonderful caviar!

meanings.note: Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (stem 'стоять'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'wait', paired with 'стоять'.

examples.text: Если о чём-то постоянно думать, это обязательно произойдёт.
examples.trans: If you think about something constantly, it will definitely happen.
Wait, don't go!
I'll stand here for a bit.

meanings.en: to hear out, listen attentively to
meanings.note: Prefix 'вы-' ('out of') marks outward movement or thorough completion (stem 'слушать'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to listen to, hear out', paired with 'выслушивать'.

examples.trans: Lena, wait, hear me out!
First listen to me very carefully.
The judge patiently heard out the witness's testimony.

meanings.en: must, need to, it is necessary
meanings.note: Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.

examples.trans: You should watch where you are going!

examples.text: А в номере над кухней пахнет точно так же. Что-то с вентиляцией.
examples.trans: And in the room above the kitchen it smells the exact same way. Something is wrong with the ventilation.
There is no need to explain anything.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'nothing', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: There is no need to explain anything.
There's nothing left.
I don't know anything.

meanings.note: Prefix 'об-' ('around, about') marks encirclement or comprehensive action (stem 'ъяснять'). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to explain'.

examples.trans: There is no need to explain anything.

examples.text: Надо всё сделать и объяснять вовремя.
examples.trans: We need to do everything and to explain on time.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian conversational adverb meaning 'for nothing, in vain', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Не зря вас советуют! Так приятно.
examples.trans: It is not for nothing that people recommend you! So pleasant.
You're wasting your time.
I came for nothing.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'you', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: В пятницу у Лёвы день рождения.
examples.trans: On Friday it is Lyova's birthday.

examples.text: Простите, я вас не заметила. Вы мне нос сломали!
examples.trans: Forgive me, I did not notice you. You broke my nose!
You should watch where you are going!

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'оветовать'). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to advise, recommend', paired with 'посоветовать'.

examples.text: Вот я как раз и советую!
examples.trans: That is exactly what I am advising!
The doctor advises resting more.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian conversational adverb meaning 'so', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Well I brought canned stewed meat.
None at all. Spartak is not playing today.

examples.text: Будущую? Я ещё не в таком статусе.
examples.trans: Future? I am not in that status yet.

meanings.note: Prefix 'при-' indicates approaching, attachment, or slight degree of action (stem 'ятный'). Adjective formed with the common Slavic suffix '-н-' from a noun/verb root. Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('pleasant').

examples.trans: Thank you very much, that is very nice.

examples.text: Не зря вас советуют! Так приятно.
examples.trans: It is not for nothing that people recommend you! So pleasant.
Enjoy your meal!

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'who', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Кто-нибудь знает, где здесь ближайший ювелирный магазин?
examples.trans: Does anyone know where the nearest jewelry store is around here?
Viktoriya Sergeyevna, are you comfortable?

examples.text: Егор, слушай, Виктория Сергеевна попросила отнести это вино в номер, который она сняла.
examples.trans: Yegor, listen, Viktoriya Sergeyevna asked me to take this wine to the room she booked.

meanings.en: to put, to place, to lay down
meanings.note: Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (stem 'ложить'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'put, added', paired with 'класть'.

examples.trans: Who put a ring in here?!

examples.text: В гроб с собой икру не положишь!
examples.trans: You can't put caviar in your coffin to take with you!
Put the keys on the table.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian conversational adverb meaning 'here', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Who put a ring in here?!
Give me the keys.
Come here!

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'пина'). Common feminine noun meaning 'back' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: My back hurts, it is awful!

examples.text: Извините, спину свело. Моё положение никак не повлияет на работу.
examples.trans: Excuse me, my back cramped up. My condition will not affect my work in any way.

examples.text: Конечно, очень сильные боли и в шее, и в спине.
examples.trans: Of course, very strong pains in both the neck and the back.

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'овсем').

examples.trans: My back is completely better, thank you!

examples.text: Я совсем не это хочу сказать.
examples.trans: That's not what I mean at all.
He's completely alone.

пройти.gloss: to go through, to pass; to come along

meanings.note: Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to go through, to pass; to come along', paired with 'проходить'.

related.gloss: not to to go through (negated infinitive)

examples.text: Но вы не волнуйтесь. Массаж снимет боль, и боли в спине пройдут.
examples.trans: But do not worry. The massage will relieve the ache, and the back pains will pass.
Go through, please.
Then it passes.

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'пасибо'). Common neuter noun meaning 'thank you' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: Thank you. Sorry that I bothered you.
Thank you for the stewed meat.
Thank you for giving me a ride.
